title: The pink that wasn't for us
excerpt: Jaipur's famous pink walls were painted for a visiting British prince in 1876. The city kept the colour long after the prince left.
body:
In 1876, Maharaja Ram Singh II ordered the entire old city of Jaipur to be painted pink — the colour of hospitality — to welcome the Prince of Wales. The prince came, was suitably impressed, and left.

The colour stayed.

Today, it is law: buildings in the walled city must be painted pink. The shade has deepened over a century of repainting until it is something richer than the original.

"We paint it every year before Diwali," says Hemraj, whose family has been painting havelis in the old city for three generations. "The original was for the British. This one is ours."
